title: Pin the Step 7 oracle replay to an OpenBLAS kernel so CI can check it
summary: The Step 7 oracle test failed on the GitHub runners while passing on the capture machine: 13747 of 15300 state values differed, from 7e-14 at control 1 growing to 8e-4. NumPy's bundled OpenBLAS picks its kernel by CPU, and the kernels round differently; forcing OPENBLAS_CORETYPE=Haswell on the capture machine reproduces the runner failure exactly. step7_baseline_20261013_001 had used the AVX-512 SkylakeX kernel: a recapture at main 7478fca8 with that kernel reproduces its trajectory.npz byte for byte. A second capture at the same commit with the AVX2 Haswell kernel, step7_baseline_haswell_20261027_001 (state SHA-256 bbcef80123d1d064ce07c1aabae61ea1dd35f2c907d7e1f2a8603b5dcef16d1a), has the same source files, protocol, resets and counters. The test now replays each oracle in a subprocess pinned to its kernel on one OpenBLAS thread and still requires exact equality: the Haswell oracle runs on any x86-64 host, and the original runs where the CPU has AVX-512. A replay of the Haswell oracle on the SkylakeX kernel fails, so the pin takes effect. The original fixture stays unchanged. Surrogate runs are bit-reproducible per OpenBLAS kernel, not across machines.
next: Bring the Step 7 CPU comparison and its open questions to the first #67 review on PR #94.
reason: A test fixture and replay harness for the CPU surrogate: no physics, native run, admission or accepted capability changes.
